concepts.name: The Meaning Of Globalization • Globaliza
concepts.simple_definition: The meaning of globalization • Globalization refers to the multiplicity of linkages and interconnections between the states and societies which make up the modern world system
concepts.deep_explanation: It describes the process by which events, decisions, and activities in one part of the world can come to have significant consequences for individuals and communities in quite distant parts of the globe
concepts.real_example: Practical example of The meaning of globalization • Globaliza from page 174.
concepts.common_confusion: Students sometimes confuse The meaning of globalization • Globaliza with adjacent topics in Chapter 8.
concepts.simple_definition_amharic: [አማርኛ] The meaning of globalization • Globalization refers to the multiplicity of linkages and interconnections between the states and societies which make up the modern world system (ይህ ትርጓሜ በኢትዮጵያ የ10ኛ ክፍል ሥርዓተ-ትምህርት መሠረት የተዘጋጀ ነው)።

concepts.name: Dimensions Of Globalization The Process
concepts.simple_definition: Dimensions of globalization The process of globalization is a combination of economic, social, cultural and political dimensions or elements
concepts.deep_explanation: Political dimensions of globalization: refers to the intensification and expansion of political interrelations across the globe for different purposes

concepts.name: Globalization Has Both Advantages And Di
concepts.simple_definition: Globalization has both advantages and disadvantages (positive and negative effects) Its advantage and disadvantage depends on the way governments of the world manage it
concepts.deep_explanation: If countries manage it effectively to seize the opportunities, globalization will have positive effects/advantages

concepts.name: Globalization Of Mass Media Leads To Mul
concepts.simple_definition: globalization of mass media leads to multiculturalism
concepts.deep_explanation: The growth of cross-cultural contacts; advent of new categories of consciousness and identities such as Globalism - which embodies cultural diffusion, the desire to consume and enjoy foreign products and ideas, adopt new technology and practices, and participate in a “world culture’, for example, the trading of coffee, which is said to be originally from Ethiopia, and consumed in many parts of the world
